title: Rav Dimi bar Chinena (II)
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He was younger than Rava, and he had a brother named Ravin, as in [Bava Batra 13b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.13b.7): Ravin bar Chinena and Rav Dimi bar Chinena — their father left them two maidservants … they came before Rava.

This Rav Dimi is mentioned in [Eruvin 61a](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.61a.18-19), disagreeing with Rav Safra; in [Bava Kamma 98b:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.98b.2) he said, “This of Rabbah is a dispute of Rabbi Shimon,” etc., and Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua [objects](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.98b.3);[^4] in [Sanhedrin 84b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.84b.13) he disagrees with Rav Mattenah and says: “Just as one who strikes an animal for healing is exempt, so one who strikes a person for healing is exempt.” His brother Ravin lived also in Rav Ashi’s time, as in [Pesachim 109b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.109b.2).[^3]

notes.text: פריך means raising an objection, not necessarily successfully refuting the position. The first and second Rav Dimi entries are not merged, and the brothers’ father and chronological inference remain the supplied account.
Rav Dimi II remains distinct from Rav Dimi I; an objection by Rav Huna does not itself establish a successful refutation.

Bava Batra names the two brothers and distinguishes the skills of the two inherited servants. Eruvin assigns the two alternatives to Dimi and Safra collectively in one version. In Pesachim, Rav Ashi reports what Ravin said to him.

The linked Bavli gives the name Dimi bar Chanina. He applies the dispute between Rabbi Shimon and the Sages to a promissory note that was burned. Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua challenges that comparison.
